title: Senator Rick Scott reintroduces resolution honoring July 11 Cuban pro-democracy movement
text:
Senator Rick Scott reintroduces resolution honoring July 11 Cuban pro-democracy movement
Senator Rick Scott announced on July 15 the reintroduction of a Senate resolution to honor those who participated in the July 11, 2021, pro-democracy demonstrations in Cuba and to condemn the Cuban communist regime. The announcement comes five years after what Scott described as the largest prodemocracy uprising in Cuba in over six decades.
Scott said thousands of peaceful protesters were arrested, beaten, and imprisoned for demanding freedom and rights. "Fue el mayor levantamiento prodemocracia en Cuba en más de seis décadas, un recordatorio contundente de que el deseo de libertad del pueblo cubano nunca podrá extinguirse," he said.
According to Scott, despite ongoing repression by the Cuban government, "el espíritu del movimiento del 11 de julio sigue vivo e inspirando a millones de personas amantes de la libertad en Florida, Estados Unidos y el mundo." He stated that alongside Senator Ashley Moody he has reintroduced a resolution to honor those who stood up on July 11 and to condemn what he called the illegitimate communist regime. "Se lo debemos a cada preso político, a cada familia perseguida y a cada cubano que aún sueña con la libertad, asegurar que su sacrificio nunca sea olvidado," Scott said.
Scott also addressed changes in U.S. policy toward dictatorships in Latin America: "Hoy, la marea ha cambiado. Los dictadores que creían que podían actuar impunemente están aprendiendo que enfrentarse a la justicia ya no es opcional." He referenced recent actions such as the Department of Justice's prosecution of former Cuban leader Raúl Castro for his alleged role in an attack on civilian aircraft.
The senator emphasized his continued legislative efforts including support for measures like his DEMOCRACIA Act and legislation to restrict visas for individuals benefiting from authoritarian regimes. He said, "Sigo luchando para aprobar mi Ley DEMOCRACIA... A principios de este año también reintroduje la Ley de No Ayuda para Aliados de Dictadores para revocar y negar visados estadounidenses..."
Scott concluded by reaffirming commitment to denying resources to the current Cuban government and holding accountable anyone who supports it: "Seguiré trabajando junto al Presidente Trump... para negar al régimen los recursos que utiliza para oprimir a su pueblo y para responsabilizar a todos los que ayudan a mantenerlo en el poder."
Scott champions fiscal responsibility, debt reduction and policies supporting families and small businesses; served on active duty in the U.S. Navy; earned degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City and Southern Methodist University; serves on several Senate committees; won election representing Florida; and with his wife Ann raised two daughters—all according to the official website.
